owner.occupation: Music therapist working with refugee children

world.bio: Music therapist at a small nonprofit in Moabit. I run weekly groups for Arabic-speaking children aged six to twelve, most of them living in nearby shelters or newly rehoused flats. We sing, drum, and improvise; words come later, if at all. I keep a cupboard of mismatched donated instruments and I know every one of them by its flaws.
skills_assets: Master's in music therapy (Berlin, UDK), four years of clinical practice with children
Runs three weekly groups with about eight children each
A cupboard of donated instruments: hand drums, a kalimba, two xylophones, two ouds, a battered keyboard
Basic Arabic greetings and about two hundred song titles
Access to the nonprofit's instrument and supplies budget, which I administer
Quiet room in the nonprofit's building with a good floor for drum circles

projects.name: Thursday group, Moabit
projects.text: Eight children, mostly Syrian and Iraqi, some Afghan. We open with a hello song and end with a lullaby in Arabic that one girl taught us. Several kids in her group recognise the oud from home: when I put the donated oud on the floor, three of them went silent and one tried to play it lying on his stomach. The two donated ouds are adult-sized, and one has a cracked soundboard, so the children can't actually hold them.

projects.name: Year-end instrument budget
projects.text: The nonprofit has €3,000 left in this year's instrument budget and I have to commit it before December or it disappears into the general pot. I've been drafting a list: a better sound system, two more hand drums, a set of Orff instruments. Nothing on that list is what the children asked for.

notes.text: Thursday group. Rana, who is nine, asked me in Arabic what the big sad guitar was and I realised she meant the oud. She said her uncle had one. She didn't say where her uncle is now. I didn't ask.

The cracked oud again. I took it home to look at under proper light; the soundboard crack runs about fifteen centimetres from the bridge. Glue won't hold it. I know nothing about luthiery. Told my colleague Jonas and he said to throw it out. I couldn't.
Half-marathon training: ten kilometres along the Spree, knees fine, mood grim. The mould in the bathroom has come back. Landlord's answer is 'ventilate more', which is what they say about everything.
Arabic lesson, lesson eleven. I can now say 'where does it hurt' and 'do you want to play' and, more usefully, 'we can wait'. My teacher says I roll my r's like a Berliner. Cheers.

Finance meeting. We have about €3,000 left in the instrument line. Mara in accounts says unspent budget doesn't roll over. I wrote 'child-sized ouds??' on my notepad and then crossed it out because I don't know what that costs or who makes them.

A hard session. A boy who never speaks played the same single drum beat for twenty minutes, and then stopped and cried. We sat. His caseworker says the family may be moved again in November. I try not to build too much in the group because it can vanish, but I do anyway.
Run, then pancake brunch with my sister. She asked when I'm going to take a proper holiday. I said when the budget is spent. She rolled her eyes.
Looked up oud shops online. A lot of beautiful instruments in Istanbul and Cairo, very expensive. Nothing child-sized. One forum post said children usually start on a 'short-scale' oud, a rare thing.
Supervision. My supervisor asked what I need. I said, honestly, a few more hours of sleep and an instrument the kids can hold. She laughed and said the second one is easier.

messages.text:
Jonas: The cracked oud is taking up half the cupboard.
Me: I know. I'm not binning it.
Jonas: Put it on the shelf, then, as an exhibit.

Mara: Reminder, instrument line is €3,000 till year end.
Me: Can it go to an external repair or commission?
Mara: Yes, with two quotes.

Ayman: Thank you for the music. My son sings at home now.
Me: He's wonderful. He asked for the oud again on Thursday.
Ayman: My father played. Maybe someday.

Lena: Half marathon in two weeks?
Me: Three. Don't remind me.
Lena: Come to dinner after, I'll make the lentil thing.

Agent: Regarding the mould: a technician will inspect on the 12th.
Me: Please confirm time.
Agent: Between 8 and 12.

relations.about: Syrian family in a shelter near Turmstraße; the uncle played oud.
Colleague, social worker, kind but practical about the cupboard of old instruments.
Wise, tells me to do small things.

constraints: Can only spend the nonprofit's budget with two written quotes
Child safety and consent rules for any visitor
Not able to take on unpaid extra work during marathon training
sensitive: Stress about children whose families might be moved
Burnout creeping in; sleep is poor
